newsitem.title: CHINA: China insurer to pay $385 million in flood damage.
newsitem.headline: China insurer to pay $385 million in flood damage.

text.p: China's big insurer, the People's Insurance Group, expects to pay out 3.2 billion yuan ($385.5 million) in damage claims for widespread flooding this summer, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The People's Insurance (Property) Co of China Ltd had already paid out 800 million yuan in claims as of August 20 and the extent of the damage was still being tallied, the newspaper quoted a company official as saying.
Flooding across large sections of southern, central and northeastern China had killed at least 2,700 people, injured more than 32,200 and caused more than 52.4 billion yuan of damages this year.
In northern Hebei province, the company had paid more than 2,400 enterprises and 15,000 families a total of 51 million yuan, said the official, who was not named.
Insured losses were only a fraction of the total flood damage, he said. Many people in China, particularly in rural areas, do not bother with insurance.
Losses in central Hubei province had been estimated at 11.2 billion yuan, of which just 260 million yuan was covered by insurance, he said.
More than 1.38 million people in five provinces were evacuated last month after record rainfalls and flash floods destroyed 1.125 million homes and damaged 1.85 million others.
Typhoons that battered the southeastern province of Fujian left more than 100,000 people homeless and washed away tens of thousands of tonnes of grain from state and private stores.
Disaster control authorities have warned that water levels in rivers in central and northeast China are still dangerously high and that heavier flooding could strike in the autumn.
